item.description: - The introduction now actually appears on a first run. It was being counted as shown the moment it reached the screen rather than once you had read it, so anything that took it away first — the ⌃⌥⌘B bypass, the screen resting, quitting the app — meant it never came back. And starting an intention from the menu bar skipped it altogether, which on a fresh install is the likeliest thing to click, since there is no window. It is now counted only when you reach the end of it.

- A short introduction the first time you run Intention: four screens on what it's for, ending at your first intention. It appears only when there's no history to show — a fresh install, or after clearing your data — so it never gets in the way of anyone already using the app.
- A new Dashboard section in Settings, for people with a licence, with one thing in it: clear all recorded data and start the dashboard again from empty. It says how many sessions it's about to delete before you press it, and asks once more after. Your settings and your licence are kept.
- The menu bar item can be trimmed down, under Settings › Personalization › Menu bar item. The countdown can be turned off, leaving the menu bar naming what you're working on without a clock ticking beside it — useful if a timer in the corner of the screen is the thing you end up watching instead of the work. The icon can be turned off too, for a crowded menu bar. Either way the session is untouched and still ends at the same time.

- The dashboard licence is now bought and checked through Dodo Payments, and priced in US dollars. Nothing changes about what you get or how you enter a code. No licence had been sold under the old provider, so no existing licence is affected. - The paywall no longer quotes a price before you get to the checkout page, which is the one place that can state it correctly for where you are and what you're paying with. - An outage at the licence server no longer counts against you. A server error is now treated the same as having no connection at all — your Mac stays unlocked — where before it risked reading as a refusal. - Pasting into the dashboard or Settings works. Both windows used to take a click without bringing Intention to the front, which left ⌘V going to whichever app the menu bar still belonged to — so a pasted licence code went somewhere else entirely, with nothing on screen to say so. - The dashboard and Settings no longer sit above every other app's windows. They still stay lit while you're working elsewhere, which is the whole point of them, but now you can put something in front when you want to.
